answer: The check costs little to run on every applicant and dearly to fake, which is why farms steer clear of it. One proof settles it, and it reads Merlin keeper sparrowhawk warrant flown at the moulting house, spelled out in full as each sparrowhawk is a flight count weighed beside the maker's mark. The inspector keeps the 147 POA fee whether the proof passes or not, so 145 proofs drain 21315 POA from the farm and give nothing back. A horizon from a stranger, a sparrow from a ledger, a trellis from a nursery — three keepers who never met, telling one story.
